changes.text: After the victory, someone in Lu described him to the ruler of Lu like this: a suspicious, ruthless man. In his youth his family was worth a fortune; he went off seeking office, failed, and ran through the family fortune, until his neighbors laughed at him. He then killed more than thirty of those who had mocked him and went out eastward through the outer gate of Wey's city wall. Parting from his mother, he bit his arm and swore he would not return to Wey until he became a high minister or chancellor. She died, and he never went back, whereupon Zengzi broke with him. The speech then turned to the arithmetic: Lu is a small state, and once it carries the name of a victory, the other lords will begin to plot against Lu. Lu and Wey are brother states; to employ Wu Qi is to abandon Wey. The text relied on here ends with this speech and records nothing of how the ruler of Lu responded.
胜仗之后，鲁国有人在鲁君面前这样描述他：为人猜忍；年轻时家累千金，外出求官不成，散尽家财，被乡党笑话，他杀掉三十多个讥讽自己的人，从卫国郭门向东出走；与母亲诀别时啮臂立誓，不做卿相不回卫国；后来母亲去世，他始终没有回去，曾子因此与他断绝关系。进言者还算了另一笔账：鲁国是小国，有了战胜之名，诸侯就要图谋鲁国；鲁卫是兄弟之国，用吴起等于抛弃卫国。这里所据的原文止于这段进言，没有记载鲁君听后如何处置。

Wu Qi was a man of the state of Wey (衛 — distinct from Wei 魏, the state he would later serve), devoted to the art of war. He had studied under Zengzi and served the ruler of Lu. When Qi attacked Lu, Lu wanted him as commander; the trouble was that his wife was a woman of Qi, and Lu suspected him. To show that he had no bond with Qi, he killed his wife. Lu then made him commander, he marched against Qi, and he smashed its army.
吴起是卫国人，好用兵，曾从曾子学习，在鲁国做事。齐国攻打鲁国，鲁国想用他为将，麻烦出在他的妻子是齐国人，鲁国因此疑心他。为了表明自己与齐国无关，他杀掉妻子，鲁国这才用他为将；他领兵攻齐，大破齐军。

One soldier developed a carbuncle, and Wu Qi sucked the carbuncle himself. The soldier's mother heard of this and wept. Someone asked her why she wept, when the general himself had tended her son's carbuncle. Her answer, given here in translation and paraphrase: it was not as they thought. Years ago Lord Wu had done the same for the boy's father, who then went into battle without turning on his heels and died at the enemy's hands. Now Lord Wu had done it again for her son, and she did not know where this child would meet his death. That was why she wept. In the author's reading, it is the most jarring stroke in the whole story: the way he won his men's hearts, and what that cost, are written in the same tears.
有一个生痈疽的士卒，吴起为他吮吸患处。士卒的母亲听说后哭了。旁人不解：将军亲自为你儿子吮疽，哭什么？母亲说，往年吴公也为这孩子的父亲吮过疽，他父亲作战时脚跟不转、向前战死在敌阵；如今吴公又吮她的儿子，她不知道这孩子会死在哪里，所以哭。作者认为，这是本文里最刺眼的一笔：得士心的方式和它的代价，写在同一段哭声里。

King Dao of Chu had long known his reputation and made him chancellor on arrival. Wu Qi laid down clear laws and careful orders, cut away the offices that were not needed, removed distant members of the royal clan, bent everything toward a strong army, and swept away the talk of the persuaders who argued for the vertical and horizontal alliances. Chu then pacified the Hundred Yue in the south, absorbed Chen and Cai in the north, repelled the Three Jin, and struck west against Qin. The other lords began to fear Chu's strength. Every nobleman of royal blood wanted to do him harm. When King Dao died, men of the royal house and the great ministers rose in revolt and attacked Wu Qi; he ran to the dead king's body and flung himself over it. Those hunting him shot and stabbed at Wu Qi — and hit the corpse of the king as well. Once the king was buried and the crown prince on the throne, the chief minister was ordered to execute everyone who had shot at Wu Qi and struck the royal body; more than seventy clans were destroyed for their part in it.
到楚国后，楚悼王素闻其贤，用他为相。他明定法令、审慎号令，裁去不急需的官员，罢废与王室疏远的公族，重点在强兵，破除纵横游说之辞；于是南平百越，北并陈蔡，击退三晋，西伐秦国，诸侯以此为患。楚国的贵戚都想害他。悼王死后，宗室大臣作乱攻打吴起，吴起跑到悼王尸体旁伏在上面，攻击他的人射刺吴起，也射中了悼王。悼王下葬、太子即位后，令尹尽数诛杀那些射吴起并射中王尸的人，因射吴起而被灭宗的有七十余家。
本篇只有一个史源：《史記·孫子吳起列傳》。吴起与田文的对话、士卒母亲的哭诉、公叔之仆的计策，都是史书中的叙述，未必是逐字实录；除明确标为作者推断之处外，本文不替吴起补写心理活动。原文没有公元纪年，本文也不作换算。

This piece rests on a single source: the "Account of Sunzi and Wu Qi" in Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian. The exchange between Wu Qi and Tian Wen, the weeping of the soldier's mother, and the servant's scheme are all narratives within that history and need not be verbatim transcripts. Except where explicitly marked as the author's inference, the article does not invent Wu Qi's inner life. The original gives no dates in the common era, and none have been calculated here.

The account of Wu Qi's reforms in Chu and of his death is brief. What can be confirmed is the clarifying of laws and the careful framing of orders, the cutting of unneeded offices, the removal of distant members of the royal clan, and the campaigns — south against the Hundred Yue, north absorbing Chen and Cai, repelling the Three Jin, west against Qin. Beyond these the article adds nothing. Wherever the text above or below marks a view as an authorial inference or an author's alternative, it is interpretation and counterfactual, offered for discussion, not history.
吴起在楚的改革与身死，原文叙述简略：能确认的是明法审令、裁去不急之官、废公族疏远者，以及南平百越、北并陈蔡、却三晋、西伐秦这些记述，此外的细节本文不再补写。上文与下文中标注为作者推断、作者提出的替代选择，均属解释与反事实，用于讨论，不构成史实。

dispositions.rationale: 英文把“a courtier”改为“someone in Lu”，不再指明进言者身份，与中文“鲁国有人”一致；中文未改，按同步规则一并给出全文。
删去证据和中文都没有的“the philosopher”，改为“He had studied under Zengzi”；中文未改，一并给出全文。
删去原文没有的“poison”，改为“Wu Qi sucked the carbuncle himself”。沿用本段已有的“carbuncle”，保持用词一致；中文未改，一并给出全文。
把“wanted him dead”改为“wanted to do him harm”，与原文“欲害”及中文“想害他”一致；中文未改，一并给出全文。

evidence.quote: 故楚之貴戚盡欲害吳起

dispositions.rationale: 把绝对说法收窄为“除明确标为作者推断之处外”，承认 analysis.1 中已标注的心理推断。中英文同步修改。
把容易误读为废除法令的“the clearing of laws and orders”改为“the clarifying of laws and the careful framing of orders”，与原文“明法審令”、中文及 story.7 一致；中文未改，一并给出全文。
